shortDescription: Malaysia Aviation Group, the parent of national carrier Malaysia Airlines, will buy 10 Boeing NYSE:BA 787 Dreamliners as part of its fleet modernisation programme, its chief executive said on Wednesday.

children: Malaysia Aviation Group, the parent of national carrier Malaysia Airlines, will buy 10 Boeing
787 Dreamliners as part of its fleet modernisation programme, its chief executive said on Wednesday.
The order will include an option to buy an additional six aircraft, MAG President and CEO Nasaruddin A Bakar said at a ceremony to exchange documents
The financial terms of the deal and delivery dates were not immediately disclosed
The Dreamliner would "offer capacity, flexibility, and efficiency required to support our long-term growth", Nasaruddin said
Malaysia last year said it would purchase 30 Boeing 737 MAX narrowbody jets with the option of buying 30 more, under a trade deal agreed between Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim and US President
MAG this year cut about 6% of its capacity, or roughly 8,000 to 9,000 flights in 2026, to manage costs amid higher jet fuel prices stemming from the Middle East conflict
It plans to increase capacity by about 8% next year, Nasaruddin told Reuters earlier this month
The announcement comes a day after China Southern Airlines
said its subsidiary Xiamen Airlines had agreed to buy 50 Boeing 737 MAX 8 planes at a list price of about $7.4 billion, the largest Chinese airplane deal for the US planemaker in nearly a decade
